name: Open-PTC (daly2211/open-ptc)
pinned: 2f2ef0ce4087d338a2cd1646c8ef18cc3f57b1de (last commit 2026-04-25); run on host Deno 2.9.8; dependencies resolved with --no-lock (see surprises)
engine: A fresh `deno run` subprocess per execution (V8, Deno's own permission system: --allow-net=localhost:<rpc port>, --allow-env=RPC_SERVER_URL, nothing else). There is only this one execution mode in the code; the README's 'Deno isolate' and 'restricted Deno subprocess' describe the same subprocess.
how_run: deno run --allow-all --no-lock src/server.ts --ws (the project's own server, ports 41302 RPC / 41303 WS); the harness registers `lookup` over the WebSocket register_tools message and sends each probe as execute_code, the local-tool path used by the project's AI SDK and LangGraph examples. Sandbox code calls it as main.lookup(...).

P1.detail: printed 42, 1 host call, 234 ms round trip. The tool is reached as main.lookup (WebSocket tools are grouped under `main`).

P2.detail: Only printed output returns: all 200,000 A's came back (output = stdout + "\n\n" + stderr, 200,003 chars), no truncation and no marker. The bare last expression "RETURNED" is not returned: the code runs as a module file, so there is no return channel at all.

P3.detail: NotCapable: Requires net access to "example.com:443", run again with the --allow-net flag. Extra P3b: import("https://example.com/probe.js") -> TypeError: Requires import access to "example.com:443". Net is allowed only to localhost:<rpc port>.

P4.detail: require("fs") -> ReferenceError: require is not defined (not-defined); import("node:fs") readFileSync and Deno.readTextFile -> NotCapable: Requires read access to "/etc/hosts".

P5.detail: process.env.PROBE_SECRET and Deno.env.get -> NotCapable: Requires env access to "PROBE_SECRET"; Deno.env.toObject() -> NotCapable. The variable IS present in the subprocess env (Deno.Command merges the parent env because clearEnv is not set); only the permission flag hides it.

P6.detail: Subprocess SIGTERMed by the host timer after 30,043 ms; output ends with "[Process terminated after exceeding timeout of 30000 ms]".

P7.detail: No memory limit. The harness killed the sandbox subprocess at 4,305 MB process-tree RSS after 7.4 s (baseline 106 MB). The execution then returned success:false with empty output; the server survived and the next execution printed alive.

P8.detail: fresh: second execution printed gone (new subprocess each time).

P9.detail: 213 ms measured inside the sandbox for 5 Promise.all lookups, 5 host calls: parallel. Each callTool is an independent fetch to the RPC server.

P10.detail: success:false, output is Deno's uncaught-error text with ANSI colour codes: "error: Uncaught (in promise) Error: probe-boom", the source line, a caret, and "at file:///var/folders/.../T/<random>.ts:37:7". Message and stack survive; line numbers are offset by the prepended RPC client and proxy code (user line 3 -> 37 with one tool registered), and the host temp path leaks.

P11.detail: median 16.5 ms, p90 18 ms per execution (a new deno subprocess each, measured as WebSocket round trip). One-time setup (server start + WS connect + register) 392 ms with a warm dependency cache.

P12.detail: this.constructor.constructor(...) -> TypeError: Cannot read properties of undefined (module top-level this is undefined); (function(){return this})().process -> TypeError (strict module). globalThis.process exists (Deno's Node compat), but it is the sandbox subprocess's own process, and every capability is permission-gated: process.env -> NotCapable, Deno.Command("echo") -> NotCapable: Requires run access, node:child_process execSync -> NotCapable. No host object reached.

hardened.config: CODE_EXECUTION_TIMEOUT_MS=5000 (documented in .env.example:25-27, read at src/execution/sandbox-executor.ts:150-152). This is the only per-execution limit the project exposes; there is no memory, CPU, output or network option. The value 5000 is the harness's choice: the option takes any number. Docker Compose is documented but sets no memory or CPU limits (docker-compose.no-proxy.yml) and runs the same subprocess sandbox, so it was not used.

P3.detail: same as default: NotCapable net access to example.com:443; import also refused.

P4.detail: same as default: NotCapable read access to /etc/hosts; require not defined.

P5.detail: same as default: NotCapable env access to PROBE_SECRET.

P6.detail: terminated after 5,004 ms: "[Process terminated after exceeding timeout of 5000 ms]".

P7.detail: Stopped by the 5 s time limit, not a memory limit, after process-tree RSS reached 4,066 MB (just under the harness's 4 GB kill). Server survived; next execution printed alive. A faster allocation pattern or a longer timeout would pass 4 GB.

P9.detail: 211 ms for 5 parallel lookups, 5 host calls.

P12.detail: same as default; all five attempts blocked by TypeError or NotCapable.

defaults.time: 30,000 ms wall clock per execution (CODE_EXECUTION_TIMEOUT_MS, src/execution/sandbox-executor.ts:150-156), enforced by SIGTERM on the subprocess.
defaults.memory: None set. The subprocess gets Deno's default V8 heap; P7 reached 4.3 GB before the harness stopped it.
defaults.output: None. stdout + stderr are returned whole (sandbox-executor.ts:161-166); P2 returned 200,003 chars.
defaults.tool_calls: No count cap. WebSocket tool calls time out after 60 s each (src/ws/ws-protocol.ts WS_CONFIG.TOOL_CALL_TIMEOUT_MS). Proxy mode caps LLM chain depth at 10 (src/proxy/sandbox-orchestrator.ts:18), not tool calls.

source_notes.finding: Tools become plain objects of arrow functions generated as source text and prepended to the user code: `const <server> = { <tool>: (input) => callTool('<ref>', input) }`, with WebSocket and proxy runtime tools under `const main`. TypeScript signatures for the model come from JSON Schema via json-schema-to-typescript compile().

Two styles. MCP and REST modes expose on-demand discovery: get_tools_tree (/tree, optional descriptions and charLimit) and get_tool_signatures (/signatures filtered by serverNames/toolNames). Proxy mode instead concatenates every runtime and MCP signature into the code_executor tool description, so all schemas go in the prompt.

Sandbox code calls callTool(), which POSTs JSON-RPC to the host's RPC server over HTTP (localhost, port allowed by --allow-net). The RPC server routes by a global toolRef string: api_* to proxy sessions, main_* to WebSocket connections, anything else to MCP tools. It never checks which execution or connection made the request.

Each execution writes the code to a temp .ts file and spawns `deno run --no-prompt --allow-net=localhost:<rpc> --allow-env=RPC_SERVER_URL <file>`. The boundary is Deno's permission system in a separate OS process, not an isolate inside the server. The parent env is inherited (no clearEnv), so secrets are in the child's memory and hidden only by --allow-env. The README says 'secure Deno isolate' and 'separate Deno isolate per execution', and also says it 'should not be treated as hardened multi-tenant isolation'.

The model gets `stdout + "\n\n" + stderr + timeoutText` as one string plus a success flag (exit code 0). No return value channel, no truncation, ANSI colour codes from Deno's error printer pass through.
Only a wall-clock timeout (CODE_EXECUTION_TIMEOUT_MS, default 30000). No memory flag (no --v8-flags=--max-old-space-size), no output cap, no tool-call cap.
Fresh process per execution; nothing persists. No snapshot support.
No formatting by Open-PTC: the model sees Deno's raw uncaught-error print on stderr, including ANSI codes and the temp file path, with line numbers offset by the prepended code.

MCP server credentials are substituted from the host env into the MCP client config (${VAR}) and stay in the host process; the sandbox gets only RPC_SERVER_URL. Good separation, but the RPC server and all public servers bind 0.0.0.0 with no authentication, so anyone on the network can call tools or run code.

A second WebSocket connection's sandbox called the first connection's local `lookup` with callTool("main_<connA>.lookup", {id:50}) and got {id:50,value:100}; connection A's handler ran. Connection ids are `ws_${Date.now()}_${counter}`, so they are guessable. The README's 'namespace-isolated per WebSocket connection' holds only for the generated proxy object, not at the RPC server.

surprises: The documented start command `deno run --allow-all src/server.ts` fails at this commit: deno.json imports the unpinned `https://esm.sh/json-schema-to-typescript?target=esnext`, whose content no longer matches deno.lock (integrity check failed). The Dockerfile copies deno.json but not deno.lock, so the Docker path works. The harness ran with --no-lock to match the Docker build.

README says 'secure Deno isolate' and 'separate Deno isolate per execution'; the code spawns a separate `deno run` OS process per execution. The isolation that holds (P3, P4, P5, P12) comes from Deno permission flags, and it held in every probe.

README says local tools are 'namespace-isolated per WebSocket connection'. Sandbox code from one connection called another connection's tool by its reference name (X1), because the shared RPC server routes by name with no caller check.
No memory limit at all: one execution reached 4.3 GB in 7.4 s. The README lists memory controls under Future Improvements, so this is acknowledged.
Setting RPC_SERVER_PORT alone breaks tool calls: the executor reads RPC_SERVER_URL (default http://localhost:9732) independently, so both must be set together.
Error output carries ANSI colour escape codes and the host's temp directory path into the model's context.
